title: Reading notes: LLM inference & ICLR/NeurIPS takeaways (Summer 2025)
content:
Purpose: quick personal summary of interesting papers/blogs and conference takeaways I want to internalize and iterate on for Redwood inference work. Mostly bullets + TODOs. Informal notes for follow-ups and experiments.

High-level themes across readings (why this matters):
- Continued focus on memory/KV-cache optimizations (sparse caching, eviction policies) — directly impacts throughput/cost for long-chat workloads.
- Kernel & compiler improvements (FlashAttention v2-like techniques, fused ops) give large latency wins on both A100 and next-gen HW; good for hosted API tail.
- Quantization + activation-aware methods are maturing; need robust evals to avoid quality regressions.
- Model routing and fallbacks (smaller quantized variants) look promising as a cost/latency levers at platform level.

Notes on specific papers / posts:
1) "FlashAttention 2 / attention kernel optimizations" (paper + author posts)
- Key idea: minimize memory traffic and support larger block sizes with better tiling + numerics; reduces memory-bound attention costs.
- Implication: on our serving runtime, this could reduce token p95 by ~10-30% depending on seq len distribution.
- Open questions: compatibility with our quantized kernels and KV cache layout; does fused FlashAttention require different memory layout for KV that breaks our current prefix caching?
- Quick experiment: benchmark a small Llama-2 13B variant with FlashAtt2 kernel vs current for seq lengths 64/512/2048 on same machine (A10/A100). Compare latency, memory, and kernel fallback behavior.

2) "Efficient Transformer inference with mixed-precision and activation quantization" (blog roundup + arXiv)
- Several groups show 4-bit asymmetric quantization + small calibration sets can preserve most quality while reducing memory and increasing throughput.
- Danger: out-of-distribution prompts can trigger hallucination/quality drop. Need eval harness tied to our prod prompts.
- Action: add a small eval set derived from customer anonymized prompts (ask legal/sre) to run quantization regression checks in Redwood Optimize.

3) "Model routing & graceful degradation" (conference talk + system poster)
- Pattern: route by latency SLO and recent model quality signals; automatically downgrade to a cheaper quantized variant when capacity constrained.
- For Redwood: could integrate with existing routing policies + rollout system to do canary degradation.
- TODO: design a policy prototype name: "latency-aware degrade" that uses real-time queue length and recent per-route quality metrics.

ICLR/NeurIPS practical takeaways (short):
- More posters on real-world evals and human-centric metrics — useful for our Quality Monitoring product line.
- Several teams emphasize tying cost regressions to business metrics (e.g., time-to-first-token vs user engagement) — could be a narrative in marketing and sales decks.
- Observability: fine-grained token-level traces and per-request kernel selection logs were common. We should consider exposing a sanitized subset in Console.

Personal TODOs / experiments (short list):
- [ ] Benchmark FlashAttention2-style kernels with our runtime (ticket: INF-129). Baseline & compare across seq len. Owner: Diego. Due: 2025-08-01.
- [ ] Build a small quantization regression harness using 200 anonymized prompts. Integrate with Optimize suggestions pipeline. Owner: Maya. Due: 2025-09-01.
- [ ] Prototype "latency-aware degrade" policy in routing service; simulate traffic and measure cost/quality tradeoffs. Owner: Ryan. Due: 2025-08-15.
- [ ] Add sample notebook showing how to run per-model kernel A/B in our CI runner. Owner: Diego. Due: 2025-07-25.

Open questions / discussion points for sync with Applied ML team:
- How tightly do we want to couple kernel selection to model versioning? (tradeoff: reproducibility vs perf gains)
- What are constraints from Private/VPC deployments on shipping new kernels (e.g., binary compatibility / cert process)?
- For quantization evals, what minimum-size prompt set is representative across customer workloads?

Links & quick refs: (save here so I can copy into PRs)
- FlashAttention2 summary blog: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14165 (author blog links in my twitter bookmarks)
- Quantization survey: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.00000 (placeholder paper — check exact ref)
- Routing/capacity poster (ICLR 2025): https://twitter.com/llmconf/status/1560000000000000000

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep experiments reproducible: log kernel versions + compiler flags in benchmark artifacts.
- When testing on Dedicated vs Hosted: measure both p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-token (not just latency).
- Remember: small perf wins at kernel level multiply across our multi-tenant farms.

Meeting prep next week: want 10m with Applied ML + Runtime leads. Agenda:
- Quick summary of FlashAtt2 bench plan (5m)
- Quantization harness scope and data/legality check (3m)
- Routing policy prototype design (2m)

End of notes.
